clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old man with a 15-year history of hypertension and exposure to traditional Korean herbal medicines presented with bilateral flank pain (left onset ~1 month prior to admission, right 4 days later), dyspnea on exertion, urinary frequency, and foamy urine. One week before hospital admission, he developed bilateral floater symptoms and was diagnosed with anterior uveitis, treated with systemic and topical steroids at an ophthalmology clinic. At hospital admission, laboratory tests revealed significant renal dysfunction (BUN 26 mg/dL, serum creatinine 2.3 mg/dL, eGFR 30.9 mL/min). Slit lamp examination confirmed anterior uveitis with 1-2+ inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber bilaterally, normal fundus, and visual acuity of 20/20 right eye and 20/25 left eye. Kidney ultrasound showed elevated parenchymal echogenicity. Kidney biopsy demonstrated diffuse interstitial infiltration of lymphocytes and eosinophils with mild tubular atrophy and focal interstitial fibrosis. Electron microscopy showed no electron-dense deposits, and immunofluorescence showed no antibody deposits or immune complexes, ruling out immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis. Based on the combination of anterior uveitis and tubulointerstitial nephritis confirmed by biopsy, TINU syndrome was diagnosed. The patient was treated with topical steroid (Pred Forte), and anterior uveitis was well-controlled.

Kidney ultrasound showed elevated parenchymal echogenicity. Kidney biopsy demonstrated diffuse interstitial infiltration of lymphocytes and eosinophils with mild tubular atrophy and focal interstitial fibrosis. Electron microscopy showed no electron-dense deposits, and immunofluorescence showed no antibody deposits or immune complexes, ruling out immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis. Based on the combination of anterior uveitis and tubulointerstitial nephritis confirmed by biopsy, TINU syndrome was diagnosed. The patient was treated with topical steroid (Pred Forte), and anterior uveitis was well-controlled.

No electron-dense deposits on electron microscopy and no antibody deposits or immune complexes on immunofluorescence, ruling out immune complex-mediated disease
